title: Bhishma's vow
carry: the no and the longing, side by side

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gangeya: a son taught by the sage who cursed him, brought home as heir. Who did you thank for something they taught you? Day seven hundred ten.

A scent on the wind, sweet and strong, out by the Yamuna River. King Shantanu is walking in the woods along the bank when he catches it, and he can't tell where it comes from. So he follows it. It leads him to the water, and to a young woman with a boat, who ferries travelers across. He asks who she is. She's the daughter of the chief of the fishermen, she says, and she plies this boat at her father's bidding.
screen: `A SCENT BY THE YAMUNA.` → `THE KING FOLLOWS IT.` → `A YOUNG WOMAN WITH A BOAT.`

segments.voice: Shantanu wants to marry her. He goes to her father and asks. The fisherman doesn't refuse. He says his daughter must marry someday, and the king is welcome. But there's a condition. Promise me, he says, that the son born of her will be king after you. And Shantanu can't. He already has an heir: Devavrata, Ganga's son, the young man he brought home from the river and made heir to the throne. To promise the crown to a son not yet born would mean taking it from the son he has. So the king says nothing to the fisherman's condition, and goes home. That should be the end of it. It isn't. Back in the capital, Shantanu can't stop thinking about her. He grows quiet and withdrawn, sunk in thought, the text says, and he won't tell anyone why. This is the strange way Bhishma's vow begins: not with Bhishma, but with his father saying no. And the no is honorable. Shantanu won't disinherit his son for his own wish. But look at what he does with the no. He doesn't let it settle. He keeps the refusal and the longing side by side, and carries both in silence. Nobody in the palace knows what's wrong. The king is keeping faith with one son and grieving for one woman at the same time. And the person who will notice first is the son the no was meant to protect. The young woman's own story is still to come. For now she's only the fisherman's daughter, and a condition the king won't meet.
screen: `THE FISHERMAN'S CONDITION.` · `THE KING ALREADY HAS AN HEIR.` · `HE SAYS NO, AND GOES HOME.` · `QUIET, AND SUNK IN THOUGHT.` · then, large: `THE NO AND THE LONGING, SIDE BY SIDE.`

segments.voice: Let the breath find a slow rhythm, in and out. Bring to mind something you said no to, for a good reason, that some part of you still wants. A job, a move, a purchase, a person. Don't reopen the decision. Just let the no and the wanting sit side by side, the way Shantanu carried them. Breathe in, and feel the wanting, honestly. Breathe out, and feel the reason you said no. Neither has to win right now. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's vow. It begins with a king's refusal: he won't give his son's crown away, even for the woman he wants.
Your line: the no and the longing, side by side. Today, if you're carrying a quiet no that still hurts, name it to one person you trust. Day seven hundred ten.

howItsDone: In some Hindu marriages the families meet and talk before a match is agreed, and in some weddings the bride's father gives his daughter in a rite called kanyadana.

original.note: Sanskrit Yamunā, the river where Shantanu meets the fisherman's daughter.

trapdoor: what you thought: Bhishma's vow starts with Bhishma.
what it means: it starts with his father refusing a condition, and grieving in silence.
what a scholar hears: the fisherman's demand that his daughter's son inherit sets up everything Devavrata will vow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Shantanu meets the fisherman's daughter by the Yamuna; the fisherman's condition; the king's grief)

notes: All paraphrase. Check: the sweet scent leading Shantanu to her; her words (daughter of the fishermen's chief, plying the boat at his command); the fisherman's condition that her son be installed as successor.
The script says Shantanu 'says nothing to the condition' (Ganguli: he did not feel inclined to grant it) and returns to Hastinapura absorbed in thought; confirm.
Her name (Satyavati) is held back until her own days (716-717); the fragrance's origin is left for day 717.
Ganguli places this some years after Devavrata's installation; the script gives no number.
howItsDone describes family meetings and kanyadana generally, as things some families do; confirm.

Audit (y3, 707-716): 'hunting in the woods' became 'walking in the woods'; Ganguli has the king simply go into the woods by the Yamuna here (the hunting is days 708 and 702), and a third hunting opening in nine days was also repetitive.
